correctness.rationale: The three target inequalities on each image vertex suffice by convexity. Translating the two lower coordinate bounds to zero leaves a triangle scaled by 1−W, or an empty fiber. The W sublevel areas are r² times the footprint area, so integrating the fiber area (ab/2)(1−W)² gives ab/12 times the footprint area in ordinary Lebesgue coordinates. The gauge is coercive: a placement bounds the distance between the first two image vertices by the target diameter, so its unit sublevel is bounded, and continuity gives interior about zero. With a=t≤1=b, I checked the edge inequalities for the scaled polar normals via the exact minimum of each degree-at-most-two polynomial on [0,1], and checked eight strictly positive consecutive turns for 0<t<1. There are 25 distinct normals from the 27 indexed triples; 200 distinct edge tests therefore suffice. The supporting-line intersections and shoelace sum give the claimed area f(t) and five distinct limiting vertices of a genuine pentagon at t=1. Scaling gives V=t f(t)/12 in the normalized case and the stated formula in m,M; the increasing f(t)/t proves the unique fixed-area maximizer. At fixed b=1 the right branch minus the analytic extension of the left branch is a(a−1)^3(3a²−a+3)/[48(a+1)(a²+1)], so the first two derivatives match and the third jumps by 5/32. Zero-scale maps have measure zero; no reflected placements or Haar weighting are included.

evidence: Agarwal–Amenta–Sharir and Choi–Choi study the same four-parameter feasible set and its multiplier projection. Resultary 0f26f49ae237 expresses the self-case via mixed area.

For triangular Q and L_z(x,y)=(ux−vy,vx+uy), the mixed-area formula gives W(z)=MA(Q,L_zT)/area(Q); the gauge integral uses the ordinary multiplier measure, which in polar coordinates is scale times d(scale)d(angle).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These equivalences identify the underlying object and shared mechanism but not the aspect-ratio formula. Ordinary four-volume is not the largest feasible scale, the bare mixed area, or an unweighted angle-scale integral. An anisotropic leg rescaling conjugates a generic rotation to a nonsimilarity and does not reduce this problem to the self-case.

originality.rationale: The feasible four-polytope and its projection are known general objects, and the triangle self-containment gauge integral and equal-leg instance are known. The distinct claim is the exact fixed-source, all-right-target volume and multiplier polygon, the resulting fixed-area maximizer and the cubic derivative jump. The strongest inspected prior formulas and algorithms concern either different target/source families or a different invariant of the same polytope.
residual_risks: The negative outcome of a broad search is not evidence of novelty. Unindexed work or uninspected sections could contain an equivalent specialization.
The related same-day rectangle records do not establish a within-day priority ordering.

value.rationale: Knowing the largest similarity does not quantify the size of the feasible set. The exact ordinary volume over a full one-parameter shape family yields a normalized measure of containment and a sharp area-constrained shape comparison. The loss of footprint vertices exactly at equality and a cubic, rather than first-order, smoothness break give a concrete geometric benchmark for parametric polytope volume calculations.
residual_risks: Does not classify the full four-dimensional face lattice or extend the optimum to all triangle targets or other source shapes.
